source_name: Privátbankár.hu (Klasszis Média group)
why_relevant: Retail-finance business daily; covers bank product launches and digital channel changes, which are the visible surface of underlying vendor projects. Same publisher group as Piac & Profit and Mfor, so one crawl covers three titles' banking output.

source_name: Piac & Profit (piacesprofit.hu) — 'beszállító' tag
why_relevant: SME-business magazine with an explicit 'beszállító' (supplier) tag index — a ready-made supplier-relationship feed that occasionally covers financial-sector IT vendors and their bank clients.

source_name: Media1.hu — Hungarian media-industry watchdog
why_relevant: Tracks ownership changes and editorial-independence shifts among the very outlets in this cell (e.g. reported the acquisition of the Mfor / Privátbankár / Piac & Profit publisher). Essential for scoring the credibility and bias of each press source over time.

source_name: Bankmonitor.hu / Bank360.hu — retail bank comparison portals
why_relevant: Comparison portals reconstruct bank-by-bank obligations and rollouts in operational detail — e.g. publishing the settlement-level list of which bank must install which ATM under the 2025 MNB rule. That is direct demand-signal intelligence for cash-automation and self-service vendors.

source_name: Mindspire banki transzformációs blog
why_relevant: Hungarian banking-transformation consultancy publishing periodic status reviews of core-banking replacement projects across the domestic market — effectively an analyst-grade tracker of which HU bank is at which stage of a core renewal, written by people inside those programmes.

source_name: Bankár Magazin (bankarmagazin.hu)
why_relevant: Hungarian-language banking trade magazine; plausible carrier of executive interviews and sector-technology features in this cell. Encountered in search results but not yet content-verified for vendor-level detail.

source_name: Biztosdöntés.hu — banking/fintech news section
why_relevant: Financial comparison/news site that republishes and expands on bank digitalisation and ATM-regulation stories; useful as a redundancy layer for capturing items missed on the primary outlets.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Tagjaink (Hungarian Banking Association member list)
why_relevant: Canonical enumeration of the Hungarian credit-institution universe (~60-70 entries: banks, mortgage banks, branches of foreign banks, plus associated members/observers such as GIRO Zrt., KELER, BISZ, Magyar Államkincstár, OBA and sector sub-associations). Single best seed list for the banking actor map and for snowballing to each bank's own site.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Munkacsoportok (working groups)
why_relevant: Working-group roster reveals where the sector's technical agenda sits: Bankkártya munkacsoport (cards), Pénzforgalmi (PAD) + SEPA munkacsoport, Készpénzforgalmi munkacsoport, Digitalizációs munkacsoport, Treasury. Names the topics banks are jointly solving — a leading indicator of upcoming procurement/tender themes in payments and digital channels.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség – Kommunikék, publikációk és állásfoglalások
why_relevant: Position papers, consultation responses and the association's periodical (Gazdaság és Pénzügy) pre-announce sector direction — instant payments, digital ID, cash-handling obligations, AI — before individual banks act. Also carries long-form retrospectives (e.g. the 'Bankszövetségi Krónikák' volume on digital transition).

source_name: IVSZ – Digitális Vállalkozások Szövetsége, tagvállalatok directory
why_relevant: The largest Hungarian ICT-supplier directory (~19 pages of members, several hundred companies), filterable by size tagozat (Mikro/KKV/Nagyvállalati/Multi/Társult) and sector tagozat (Informatikai, Digitális, Startup és Scale-up, Telekommunikációs). This is the primary way to enumerate small local IT integrators and software houses that serve banks but never surface in English-language search.

source_name: IVSZ – Hírek (new-member announcements feed)
why_relevant: IVSZ publishes named 'new members joined' posts (e.g. evoCRM, Sense/Net, SimpLEGAL, Sonrisa, Ukatemi) with a one-paragraph capability description each. This is an incremental, dated feed of newly visible Hungarian technology suppliers — cheaper to monitor than re-scraping the whole directory and gives positioning language straight from the vendor.

source_name: Hungarian Fintech Association – annual Hungarian Fintech Report
why_relevant: The association publishes an annual English-language report mapping the domestic fintech ecosystem, its key players, regulatory changes and trend themes (blockchain, ESG, generative AI). Effectively a curated, citable actor map plus narrative on where the market is heading — usable both as a source and as a cross-check on our own actor list.

source_name: HVCA – Magyar Kockázati- és Magántőke Egyesület, Tagok
why_relevant: ~70 members (28 full, 32 associate, 10 individual) categorised by role, incl. an /category/investors view listing fund managers (Hiventures, FundWise, Impact Ventures, Integral Venture Partners, Hodler). Associate members are typically the law/advisory/tech service layer. Identifies who funds Hungarian fintechs — funding events are the earliest signal of a new competitor or an emerging partner.

source_name: MKIK KNYR – kamarai gazdálkodó szervezetek lekérdezhető nyilvántartása
why_relevant: Chamber membership is mandatory-registration in Hungary, so the KNYR national searchable registry is effectively a near-census of active companies, queryable by county, settlement, activity field and name. Use it to resolve/verify entities found in narrower association directories and to sweep for financial-IT activity codes not covered by any association.

source_name: Területi kereskedelmi és iparkamarák – regisztrált vállalkozói adatbázisok (county chamber company databases)
why_relevant: Each county chamber republishes its own filterable registered-company database (county, city, activity, name) and business partner-search pages. These regional cuts surface small local IT/POS service firms outside Budapest that neither IVSZ nor fintech associations list.

source_name: BKIK – Budapesti Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara, tagozatok / osztályok
why_relevant: Budapest chamber is where most financial-sector suppliers are seated. Its sectional structure includes a Gazdasági Szolgáltatások Tagozat with an Általános Pénzügyi Szolgáltatás Osztály — a ready-made segmentation of financial-services firms in the capital, plus event and committee listings that name active companies.

source_name: Magyar Lízingszövetség – tagok és pártoló tagok
why_relevant: 36 member asset-financing companies (leasing arms of banks + independent financial enterprises) and, crucially, a separate 'Pártoló tagok' (supporting members) page that lists their SERVICE PROVIDERS — e.g. BISZ Központi Hitelinformációs Zrt., CallTec Consulting. Supporting-member lists are the cleanest association-side view of who supplies technology and BPO to lenders. Also an associated member of Bankszövetség.

source_name: Magyar Faktoring Szövetség
why_relevant: Founded 2003; members are banks and specialised financial institutions active in factoring — a receivables-finance niche where fintech entrants (Flexibill, Péntech) and bank incumbents compete directly. Statutes and about pages name the constituent institutions; cooperation agreement with the Leasing Association links the two rosters.

source_name: Digitális Kereskedelmi Szövetség (DKSZ)
why_relevant: Newer digital-commerce alliance whose named participants include Mastercard, Google, DHL Express, PwC, IVSZ, Growww Digital, Boxy and Oander — i.e. it directly documents a card-scheme/consultancy/e-commerce partnership cluster. Its academies and mentor programmes surface which vendors are educating Hungarian merchants (a proxy for go-to-market pushes).

source_name: Blockchain Magyarország Egyesület – Magyar Blockchain Térkép
why_relevant: An explicit, published MAP of Hungarian blockchain/DLT actors — the association curates the ecosystem rather than just its own members. Founding member of the Blockchain Koalíció, consortium member of the DigitalTech EDIH, and affiliated to INATBA, so its pages also link outward to coalition rosters and EU digital-innovation-hub partner lists.

source_name: Mesterséges Intelligencia Koalíció – alapító tagok jegyzéke (Digitális Jólét Program)
why_relevant: A published, numbered founder-member roster of the national AI Coalition — a cross-sector list mixing banks, telcos, IT integrators and universities in one PDF. Coalition rosters like this are the classic 'small local players invisible to search' harvest, and AI working groups are where bank-side automation vendors self-identify.

source_name: Magyarország Fintech Stratégiája – a hazai pénzügyi szektor digitalizációja (Digitális Jólét Program)
why_relevant: National fintech strategy document produced with industry-association consultation; sets the policy frame that association working groups and member banks respond to, and typically names participating institutions and consultative bodies. Useful as a pointer to which associations sit at the policy table.

source_name: NJSZT – Neumann János Számítógéptudományi Társaság, szervezeti és támogatói tagság
why_relevant: The oldest Hungarian ICT professional society; its corporate/supporting membership page plus a high-frequency newsletter enumerate IT companies, research groups and universities. Complements IVSZ by capturing the academic-industrial and legacy-systems side (including banking-IT veterans) rather than the commercial-lobby side.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Kereskedelmi Szövetség (MNKSZ) – Tagjaink
why_relevant: Retail-trade association with an explicit member page and a standing e-kereskedelem topic area. Retailers are the acceptance side of payments (POS terminals, online cash registers, instant-payment acceptance obligations), so this roster identifies the buyer universe for payment-acceptance vendors.

source_name: IPAR 4.0 Nemzeti Technológiai Platform – tagszervezetek
why_relevant: A cross-sector national technology platform whose member list includes associations themselves (IVSZ is listed) alongside companies and research institutes. Platform/cluster rosters like this are second-order pointers: they enumerate the associations to sweep, and catch industrial-IT suppliers who also sell to financial back offices.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (hu.wikipedia) – history, membership and organisational overview
why_relevant: Secondary but useful for glossary/alias building and historical continuity (predecessor names, mergers such as the MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék consolidation into MBH). Not authoritative on current membership — use only to normalise names and catch defunct/renamed entities encountered in archives.
